verses.zh: 西底家背叛巴比伦王。他作王第九年十月初十日，巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒率领全军来攻击耶路撒冷，对城安营，四围筑垒攻城。
verses.en: So King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army and set up camp outside[NOTE:1] it. They built siege ramps all around it. He arrived on the tenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “against.”
This would have been Jan 15, 588 b.c. The reckoning is based on the calendar that begins the year in the spring (Nisan = March/April).

verses.zh: 于是城被围困，直到西底家王十一年。
verses.en: The city remained under siege until King Zedekiah’s eleventh year.

verses.zh: 四月初九日，城里有大饥荒，甚至百姓都没有粮食。
verses.en: By the ninth day of the fourth month[NOTE:1] the famine in the city was so severe the residents[NOTE:2] had no food.
notes: According to modern reckoning that would have been July 18, 586 b.c. So the attack against Jerusalem lasted approximately thirty months. The siege was briefly interrupted after about a year due to the arrival Egyptian forces (Eze 17:15-17; Jer 37:5-11), an inadequate force sent by Pharaoh Hophra. The final siege leading to starvation conditions thus lasted about fifteen to eighteen months.tn The MT has simply “of the month,” but the parallel passage in Jer 52:6 has “fourth month,” and this is followed by almost all English translations. The word “fourth,” however, is not actually present in the MT of 2 Kgs 25:3.
Heb “the people of the land.”

verses.zh: 城被攻破，一切兵丁就在夜间从靠近王园两城中间的门逃跑。迦勒底人正在四围攻城，王就向亚拉巴逃走。
verses.en: The enemy broke through the city walls,[NOTE:1] and all the soldiers tried to escape. They left the city during the night.[NOTE:2] They went through the gate between the two walls, which is near the king’s garden.[NOTE:3] (The Babylonians were all around the city.) Then they headed for the rift valley.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the city was breached.”
The Hebrew text is abrupt here: “And all the men of war by the night.” The translation attempts to capture the sense.

The king’s garden is mentioned again in Neh 3:15 in conjunction with the pool of Siloam and the stairs that go down from the City of David. This would have been in the southern part of the city near the Tyropean Valley which agrees with the reference to the “two walls” which were probably the walls on the eastern and western hills.

The rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿarabah) extends northward of the Dead Sea past Galilee and southward to the Gulf of Aqaba. Here the southern part of the Jordan Valley is in view with the intention to escape across the Jordan river to Moab or Ammon. It appears from Jer 40:14; 41:15 that the Ammonites were known to harbor fugitives from the Babylonians.

verses.zh: 迦勒底的军队追赶王，在耶利哥的平原追上他；他的全军都离开他四散了。
verses.en: But the Babylonian army chased after the king. They caught up with him in the rift valley plains of Jericho,[NOTE:1] and his entire army deserted him.
notes: For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.sn The rift valley plains of Jericho refer to the parts of the Jordan Valley in the vicinity of Jericho (see HALOT 880 s.v. עֲרָבָה). There the terrain is fairly level and slopes gently down to the Jordan, a descent of about 450 feet over five miles. Many translations render this as “the plains of Jericho” (ESV, NASB, NIV, KJV). See the note at Num 22:1.

verses.zh: 迦勒底人就拿住王，带他到在利比拉的巴比伦王那里审判他。
verses.en: They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah,[NOTE:1] where he[NOTE:2] passed sentence on him.
notes: Riblah was a strategic town on the Orontes River in Syria. It was at a crossing of the major roads between Egypt and Mesopotamia. Pharaoh Necho had earlier received Jehoahaz there and put him in chains (2 Kgs 23:33) prior to taking him captive to Egypt. Nebuchadnezzar had set up his base camp for conducting his campaigns against the Palestinian states there and was now sitting in judgment on prisoners brought to him.
The Hebrew text has the plural form of the verb, but the parallel passage in Jer 52:9 has the singular.

verses.zh: 在西底家眼前杀了他的众子，并且剜了西底家的眼睛，用铜链锁着他，带到巴比伦去。
verses.en: Zedekiah’s sons were executed while Zedekiah was forced to watch.[NOTE:1] The king of Babylon[NOTE:2] then had Zedekiah’s eyes put out, bound him in bronze chains, and carried him off to Babylon.
notes: Heb “were killed before his eyes.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the king of Babylon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒十九年五月初七日，巴比伦王的臣仆、护卫长尼布撒拉旦来到耶路撒冷，
verses.en: On the seventh[NOTE:1] day of the fifth month,[NOTE:2] in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard,[NOTE:3] who served the king of Babylon, arrived in Jerusalem.[NOTE:4]
notes: The parallel account in Jer 52:12 has “tenth.”
The seventh day of the month would have been August 14, 586 b.c. in modern reckoning.
For the meaning of this phrase see BDB 371 s.v. טַבָּח 2, and compare the usage in Gen 39:1.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 用火焚烧耶和华的殿和王宫，又焚烧耶路撒冷的房屋，就是各大户家的房屋。
verses.en: He burned down the Lord’s temple, the royal palace, and all the houses in Jerusalem, including every large house.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and every large house he burned down with fire.”

verses.zh: 跟从护卫长迦勒底的全军就拆毁耶路撒冷四围的城墙。
verses.en: The whole Babylonian army that came with the captain of the royal guard tore down the walls that surrounded Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 那时护卫长尼布撒拉旦将城里所剩下的百姓，并已经投降巴比伦王的人，以及大众所剩下的人，都掳去了。
verses.en: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the royal guard, deported the rest of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.[NOTE:1]
notes: The MT has “the multitude.” But הֶהָמוֹן (hehamon) should probably be emended to הֶאָמוֹן (heʾamon). See Jeremiah 52:15.

verses.zh: 但护卫长留下些民中最穷的，使他们修理葡萄园，耕种田地。
verses.en: But he[NOTE:1] left behind some of the poor of the land and gave them fields and vineyards.
notes: Heb “the captain of the royal guard.” However, the subject is clear from the preceding and contemporary English style would normally avoid repeating the proper name and title.

verses.zh: 耶和华殿的铜柱，并耶和华殿的盆座和铜海，迦勒底人都打碎了，将那铜运到巴比伦去了，
verses.en: The Babylonians broke the two bronze pillars in the Lord’s temple, as well as the movable stands and the big bronze basin called “The Sea.”[NOTE:1] They took the bronze to Babylon.
notes: Heb “the bronze pillars that were in the Lord’s house and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the Lord’s house the Babylonians broke.”sn See the note at 1 Kgs 7:23.

verses.zh: 又带去锅、铲子、蜡剪、调羹，并所用的一切铜器，
verses.en: They also took the pots, shovels,[NOTE:1] trimming shears,[NOTE:2] pans, and all the bronze utensils used by the priests.[NOTE:3]
notes: These shovels were used to clean the altar.
These were used to trim the wicks.
Heb “with which they served [or, ‘fulfilled their duty’].”

verses.zh: 火鼎、碗，无论金的银的，护卫长也都带去了。
verses.en: The captain of the royal guard took the golden and silver censers[NOTE:1] and basins.
notes: These held the embers used for the incense offerings.

verses.zh: 所罗门为耶和华殿所造的两根铜柱、一个铜海，和几个盆座，这一切的铜，多得无法可称。
verses.en: The bronze of the items that King Solomon made for the Lord’s temple—including the two pillars, the big bronze basin called “The Sea,” the twelve bronze bulls under “The Sea,”[NOTE:1] and the movable stands—was too heavy to be weighed.
notes: The MT lacks “the twelve bronze bulls under ‘the Sea,’” but these words have probably been accidentally omitted by homoioarcton. The scribe’s eye may have jumped from the וְהָ (veha) on וְהַבָּקָר (vehabbaqar), “and the bulls,” to the וְהָ on וְהַמְּכֹנוֹת (vehammekhonot), “and the movable stands,” causing him to leave out the intervening words. See the parallel passage in Jer 52:20.

verses.zh: 这一根柱子高十八肘，柱上有铜顶，高三肘；铜顶的周围有网子和石榴，都是铜的。那一根柱子，照此一样，也有网子。
verses.en: Each of the pillars was about 27 feet[NOTE:1] high. The bronze top of one pillar was about 4½ feet[NOTE:2] high and had bronze latticework and pomegranate-shaped ornaments all around it. The second pillar with its latticework was like it.
notes: Heb “18 cubits.” The standard cubit in the OT is assumed by most authorities to be about 18 inches (45 cm) long.
Heb “3 cubits.” The parallel passage in Jer 52:22 has “five.”

verses.zh: 护卫长拿住大祭司西莱雅、副祭司西番亚，和三个把门的，
verses.en: The captain of the royal guard took Seraiah, the chief priest, and Zephaniah, the priest who was second in rank, and the three doorkeepers.

verses.zh: 又从城中拿住一个管理兵丁的官（或译：太监），并在城里所遇常见王面的五个人和检点国民军长的书记，以及城里遇见的国民六十个人。
verses.en: From the city he took a eunuch who was in charge of the soldiers, five[NOTE:1] of the king’s advisers[NOTE:2] who were discovered in the city, an official army secretary who drafted citizens[NOTE:3] for military service, and 60 citizens from the people of the land who were discovered in the city.
notes: The parallel passage in Jer 52:25 has “seven.”
Heb “five men seeing the king’s face.”
Heb “the people of the land.”

verses.zh: 护卫长尼布撒拉旦将这些人带到在利比拉的巴比伦王那里。
verses.en: Nebuzaradan, captain of the royal guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.zh: 巴比伦王就把他们击杀在哈马地的利比拉。这样，犹大人被掳去离开本地。
verses.en: The king of Babylon ordered them to be executed[NOTE:1] at Riblah in the territory[NOTE:2] of Hamath. So Judah was deported from its land.
notes: Heb “struck them down and killed them.”
Heb “land.”

verses.zh: 至于犹大国剩下的民，就是巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒所剩下的，巴比伦王立了沙番的孙子、亚希甘的儿子基大利作他们的省长。
verses.en: Now King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as governor over the people whom he allowed to remain in the land of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And the people who were left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left, he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.”

verses.zh: 众军长和属他们的人听见巴比伦王立了基大利作省长，于是军长尼探雅的儿子以实玛利、加利亚的儿子约哈难、尼陀法人单户蔑的儿子西莱雅、玛迦人的儿子雅撒尼亚，和属他们的人都到米斯巴见基大利。
verses.en: All the officers of the Judahite army[NOTE:1] and their troops heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah to govern. So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. The officers who came were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite.
notes: Heb “of the army.” The word “Judahite” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 基大利向他们和属他们的人起誓说：「你们不必惧怕迦勒底臣仆，只管住在这地服事巴比伦王，就可以得福。」
verses.en: Gedaliah took an oath so as to give them and their troops some assurance of safety.[NOTE:1] He said, “You don’t need to be afraid to submit to the Babylonian officials. Settle down in the land and submit to the king of Babylon. Then things will go well for you.”
notes: The words “so as to give them…some assurance of safety” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 七月间，宗室以利沙玛的孙子、尼探雅的儿子以实玛利带着十个人来，杀了基大利和同他在米斯巴的犹大人与迦勒底人。
verses.en: But in the seventh month[NOTE:1] Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who was a member of the royal family,[NOTE:2] came with 10 of his men and murdered Gedaliah,[NOTE:3] as well as the Judeans and Babylonians who were with him at Mizpah.
notes: It is not altogether clear whether this is in the same year that Jerusalem fell or not. The wall was breached in the fourth month (= early July; Jer 39:2) and Nebuzaradan came and burned the palace, the temple, and many of the houses and tore down the wall in the fifth month (= early August; Jer 52:12). That would have left time between the fifth month and the seventh month (October) to gather in the harvest of grapes, dates and figs, and olives (Jer 40:12). However, many commentators feel that too much activity takes place in too short a time for this to have been in the same year and posit that it happened the following year or even five years later when a further deportation took place, possibly in retaliation for the murder of Gedaliah and the Babylonian garrison at Mizpah (Jer 52:30). The assassination of Gedaliah had momentous consequences and was commemorated in one of the post exilic fast days lamenting the fall of Jerusalem (Zech 8:19).
Heb “[was] from the seed of the kingdom.”
Heb “and they struck down Gedaliah and he died.”

verses.zh: 于是众民，无论大小，连众军长；因为惧怕迦勒底人，都起身往埃及去了。
verses.en: Then all the people, from the youngest to the oldest, as well as the army officers, left for[NOTE:1] Egypt, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians might do.
notes: Heb “arose and went to.”

verses.zh: 犹大王约雅斤被掳后三十七年，巴比伦王以未．米罗达元年十二月二十七日，使犹大王约雅斤抬头，提他出监；
verses.en: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of King Jehoiachin of Judah, on the twenty-seventh[NOTE:1] day of the twelfth month,[NOTE:2] King Evil Merodach of Babylon, in the first year of his reign[NOTE:3], pardoned[NOTE:4] King Jehoiachin of Judah and released him[NOTE:5] from prison.
notes: The parallel account in Jer 52:31 has “twenty-fifth.”
The twenty-seventh day would be March 22, 561 b.c. in modern reckoning.

Heb “in the year of his be[coming] king” or “in the year that he began to reign.” This may be a reference to Evil Merodach’s (Amel Marduk in Babylonian) accession year, the months before New Year’s day which would mark the beginning of his first official year of kingship.
Heb “lifted up the head of.”
The words “released him” are supplied in the translation on the basis of Jer 52:31.

verses.zh: 又对他说恩言，使他的位高过与他一同在巴比伦众王的位，
verses.en: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a more prestigious position than[NOTE:1] the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
notes: Heb “made his throne above the throne of.”

verses.zh: 给他脱了囚服。他终身常在巴比伦王面前吃饭。
verses.en: Jehoiachin[NOTE:1] took off his prison clothes and ate daily in the king’s presence for the rest of his life.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Jehoiachin) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 王赐他所需用的食物，日日赐他一分，终身都是这样。
verses.en: He was given daily provisions by the king for the rest of his life until the day he died.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “until the day he died” do not appear in the MT, but they are included in the parallel passage in Jer 52:34. Probably they have been accidentally omitted by homoioteleuton. A scribe’s eye jumped from the final vav (ו) on בְּיוֹמוֹ (beyomo), “in his day,” to the final vav (ו) on מוֹתוֹ (moto), “his death,” leaving out the intervening words.
